 sync_session = sessionmaker(bind=sync_engine, expire_on_commit=False)
 
+
+@functools.cache
+def _warn_statement_binlog() -> None:
+    log.warning(
+        "binlog_format is STATEMENT, so database sessions stay at REPEATABLE READ; "
+        "concurrent writes may fail with 'Record has changed since last read'"
+    )
+
+
+def read_committed(dbapi_connection: Any, connection_record: Any) -> None:
+    """Run the session at READ COMMITTED, unless statement binary logging forbids it."""
+    cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
+    try:
+        cursor.execute("SELECT @@log_bin, @@binlog_format")
+        log_bin, binlog_format = cursor.fetchone()
+        # InnoDB refuses every write below REPEATABLE READ under STATEMENT logging.
+        if log_bin and binlog_format == "STATEMENT":
+            _warn_statement_binlog()
+        else:
+            cursor.execute("SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED")
+    finally:
+        cursor.close()
+    dbapi_connection.commit()
+
+
+# MariaDB 11.6+ at REPEATABLE READ fails a write to a row the transaction read
+# before another one committed to it (error 1020). PostgreSQL defaults to this.
+if sync_engine.dialect.name in ("mariadb", "mysql"):
+    event.listen(sync_engine, "connect", read_committed)
+
 # Disable SQLAlchemy logging as echo will print the queries
 logging.getLogger("sqlalchemy.engine.Engine").handlers = [logging.NullHandler()]

+"""Database race stubs shared by tests of concurrent writes."""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+from sqlalchemy import event
+
+from handler.database.base_handler import sync_engine
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def run_before_first(
+    prefix: str, competitor: Callable[[], object]
+) -> Iterator[list[str]]:
+    """Run `competitor` once, just before the first statement starting with `prefix`.
+
+    Yields the statements that triggered it, so a test can assert the race happened.
+    """
+    raced: list[str] = []
+
+    def before_execute(
+        conn: object,
+        cursor: object,
+        statement: str,
+        parameters: object,
+        context: object,
+        executemany: bool,
+    ) -> None:
+        if raced or not statement.lstrip().lower().startswith(prefix):
+            return
+        raced.append(statement)
+        competitor()
+
+    event.listen(sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute", before_execute)
+    try:
+        yield raced
+    finally:
+        event.remove(sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute", before_execute)

+import pytest
+
+from handler.database.base_handler import read_committed, sync_engine
+
+
+class _Cursor:
+    def __init__(self, log_bin: int, binlog_format: str) -> None:
+        self.row = (log_bin, binlog_format)
+        self.executed: list[str] = []
+
+    def execute(self, statement: str) -> None:
+        self.executed.append(statement)
+
+    def fetchone(self) -> tuple[int, str]:
+        return self.row
+
+    def close(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+class _Connection:
+    def __init__(self, cursor: _Cursor) -> None:
+        self._cursor = cursor
+        self.committed = False
+
+    def cursor(self) -> _Cursor:
+        return self._cursor
+
+    def commit(self) -> None:
+        self.committed = True
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    sync_engine.dialect.name not in ("mariadb", "mysql"),
+    reason="PostgreSQL runs at READ COMMITTED by default",
+)
+def test_sessions_run_at_read_committed():
+    with sync_engine.connect() as conn:
+        assert conn.get_isolation_level() == "READ COMMITTED"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("log_bin", "binlog_format", "sets_it"),
+    [
+        (0, "STATEMENT", True),
+        (1, "ROW", True),
+        (1, "MIXED", True),
+        (1, "STATEMENT", False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_read_committed_unless_statement_binlog(
+    log_bin: int, binlog_format: str, sets_it: bool
+):
+    cursor = _Cursor(log_bin, binlog_format)
+    connection = _Connection(cursor)
+
+    read_committed(connection, None)
+
+    set_isolation = "SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED"
+    assert (set_isolation in cursor.executed) is sets_it
+    assert connection.committed

+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+
+from tests.db_race_stubs import run_before_first
+from tests.factories import make_device_token
+
+from handler.database import db_client_token_handler
+from models.user import User
+from utils.datetime import to_utc
+
+
+def _last_used_at(token_id: int) -> datetime | None:
+    token = db_client_token_handler.get_token(token_id)
+    assert token is not None
+    return token.last_used_at
+
+
+class TestUpdateLastUsed:
+    def test_bumps_when_never_used(self, admin_user: User):
+        token, _ = make_device_token(admin_user, None)
+
+        db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(token.id)
+
+        assert _last_used_at(token.id) is not None
+
+    def test_bumps_when_last_used_is_old(self, admin_user: User):
+        old = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=10)
+        token, _ = make_device_token(admin_user, None, last_used_at=old)
+
+        db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(token.id)
+
+        refreshed = _last_used_at(token.id)
+        assert refreshed is not None
+        # MariaDB returns naive datetimes; normalize to UTC for comparison
+        assert to_utc(refreshed) > old
+
+    def test_skips_when_last_used_within_debounce_window(self, admin_user: User):
+        recent = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=1)
+        token, _ = make_device_token(admin_user, None, last_used_at=recent)
+
+        db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(token.id)
+
+        refreshed = _last_used_at(token.id)
+        assert refreshed is not None
+        assert abs((to_utc(refreshed) - recent).total_seconds()) < 1
+
+    def test_unknown_token_is_a_no_op(self):
+        db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(999_999)
+
+    def test_does_not_read_the_token_before_updating_it(
+        self, admin_user: User, executed_statements: list[str]
+    ):
+        token, _ = make_device_token(admin_user, None)
+        executed_statements.clear()
+
+        db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(token.id)
+
+        statements = [s.lstrip().lower() for s in executed_statements]
+        assert [s for s in statements if s.startswith("select")] == []
+        assert any(s.startswith("update client_tokens") for s in statements)
+
+    def test_survives_a_concurrent_request_committing_the_same_update(
+        self, admin_user: User
+    ):
+        """Guards against MariaDB error 1020, "Record has changed since last read"."""
+        token, _ = make_device_token(admin_user, None)
+
+        with run_before_first(
+            "update client_tokens",
+            lambda: db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(token.id),
+        ) as raced:
+            db_client_token_handler.update_last_used(token.id)
+
+        assert raced
+        assert _last_used_at(token.id) is not None
